title: The Burning Plain
events_chronological: In a border town, Gina, a married mother of four, meets a farmer named Nick and the two begin an affair in a trailer out in the fields.
Gina's daughter Mariana discovers the affair and follows her mother out to the trailer.
A gas leak sets the trailer alight and both Gina and Nick are killed in it.
Mariana is left to raise her younger sisters while her father drinks and blames himself.
Nick's son Santiago comes to the town to look at the wreck and to find out who the woman was.
Mariana and Santiago recognise each other and, out of grief more than anything, become lovers.
Mariana burns down her own family's house with her father's photographs inside it.
Mariana finds she is pregnant, and the two of them run away together.
Santiago is badly hurt when their car leaves the road, and Mariana is told he is dead.
Mariana gives birth to a daughter, leaves her with Santiago's family, and disappears.
Living under the name Sylvia, Mariana runs a restaurant on the northern coast, sleeps with men she does not know, and cuts herself.
Santiago, alive and badly scarred, works as a crop duster with his young daughter Maria beside him.
Santiago crashes his aircraft, and Maria is brought north by his friend Carlos to look for her mother.
Carlos finds Sylvia and tells her that Santiago is alive and that her daughter is with him.
Sylvia flies south, and mother and daughter meet each other in a hospital corridor.
syuzhet_notes: Four strands separated by up to fifteen years are cut into one another without captions, and the film's central move is to let the audience take two of them for separate women for most of the running time.
fabula_notes: The chronology is recoverable once the identity is established, from the daughter's age and the sequence of the fire, the crash and the birth.
